content.jointProblem: Can uncertainty-aware policy geolocation and spatial weather modelling identify hail-related underpricing more reliably than municipality-level loadings for Pannonia’s Vojvodina farm portfolio? The first experiment would test whether rainfall-based downscaling methods transfer to independently observed hail events, comparing spatial estimates and held-out loss predictions against municipality-level and unmodified five-kilometre-grid baselines before considering pricing integration.

rationale.text: Pejić has directly relevant experience developing field-scale weather-data pipelines for agricultural insurance in Vojvodina, providing a starting point rather than a validated hail solution.

sources.quote: RAINFIELD developed and validated a production-grade geostatistical downscaling pipeline for converting coarse-resolution satellite precipitation products into field-scale (1 km) daily rainfall grids

rationale.text: His research tests geostatistical downscaling against simpler interpolation baselines, including performance during spatially heterogeneous convective periods.

sources.quote: Leave-one-out cross-validation showed that KED reduced RMSE by 21% relative to ordinary kriging and by 34% relative to IDW, averaged across the study period.
Performance gains were most pronounced during spatially heterogeneous convective periods in June and July.

rationale.text: He has experience designing independent field-level validation rather than treating finer grid spacing as proof of accuracy.

sources.quote: These measurements were withheld from the downscaling model and used exclusively for validation.

rationale.text: His work connects spatial weather products to insurance analysis, including historical payout simulations and reproducible analysis resources.

sources.quote: A burn analysis was performed for three parametric products—sowing-period deficit, flowering-period excess, and grain-filling deficit—for maize and sunflower across 1,214 cadastral municipalities.
The archive and analysis scripts are made publicly available.

rationale.text: The selected joint-project format matches his stated interest in spatial weather products for agricultural insurance.

sources.quote: joint projects on spatial weather data products for agri-insurance or precision agriculture

constraints.text: Field-level assignment requires resolving policy locations beyond settlement names, or explicitly retaining location uncertainty; geo-tagged claims alone must not be assumed to locate the entire insured portfolio.

sources.quote: a large share of our farm addresses are stored only at the settlement level, not as coordinates.

constraints.text: The available daily, five-kilometre weather feed cannot be treated as validated field-level hail intensity. Any finer estimates require independent hail validation, not merely resampling or reliance on rainfall-validation results.

sources.quote: We do receive daily gridded weather data from MeteoVoj d.o.o. at a five-kilometre resolution
Validating precipitation downscaling products at the field level requires ground truth at sub-kilometre spacing, which standard meteorological networks cannot provide.

constraints.text: Validation must respect the limited three-year, approximately 1,200-policy dataset, with storm- or year-held-out testing and uncertainty reporting rather than treating nearby claims from the same storm as independent evidence.

sources.quote: We have three full claim years with geo-tagged loss data for about 1,200 farm policies to work with.

constraints.text: The deliverable must support automated pricing input through the existing Python batch workflow, not stop at exploratory GIS maps.

sources.quote: turning that into something that feeds the pricing model automatically is beyond what our team can do alone.
Python-based batch scoring pipeline for quarterly rating factor refresh

constraints.text: Delivery must fit limited shared company capacity, with explicit ownership for integration and maintenance; a previous mapping prototype has not reached pricing integration.

sources.quote: a four-person pricing team and a six-person IT team who split their time between operational support and new product build.
which was completed but not yet integrated into the pricing system.

risks: The demonstrated methods concern rainfall accumulation and rainfall-deficit insurance, not hail intensity or indemnity property claims. Transfer may fail; independent hail-event validation must be the first experimental gate.
Daily five-kilometre inputs may not contain enough information to recover narrow, fast-moving hail footprints. Producing a finer grid could create false precision.
Settlement-level addresses may prevent defensible field-level attribution, and geo-tagged losses may not represent the spatial distribution of all insured exposure.

Three summers may contain too few independent hailstorms for stable pricing conclusions. The reported 18% excess could also reflect insured values, vulnerability, repair costs or claims handling rather than exposure alone.
Researcher availability, access rights to suitable hail observations and station data, budget, delivery dates and data-sharing conditions remain unknown.
Limited company implementation capacity could leave another research prototype outside the production pricing workflow.
questions: What time can Pejić commit, when could the project start, and who would implement and maintain the pipeline on each side?
What budget, delivery window and acceptance criteria can the company support, including any purchase of observations or geocoding work?
Which independent hail observations are available, such as radar-derived hail products, verified event reports or hail sensors, and what are their coverage, timestamps and licensing conditions?
What variables does MeteoVoj actually supply, and does the agreement permit historical access, derived products and operational pricing use?
Can policy records be linked to cadastral parcels or insured-building coordinates, and how accurate are existing claim geotags?

Are complete historical exposure records available, including non-claiming policies, coverage periods, insured values, premiums, deductibles, crop or building characteristics, and cause-coded dated losses?
Can enough independent storms be identified for held-out evaluation, and what minimum improvement and uncertainty limits would justify proceeding beyond the pilot?
What privacy, security, actuarial review and regulatory requirements apply, and what interface must the quarterly pricing pipeline consume?
